L. Pogson. Pogson's preface is dated June 1910. The dates identify different objects; the preface date does not replace the title-page date. This digital carrier is selected for the passages below. The user's separately available local scan has not been collated with it. ## Passage locations **q001 · chapter II, displayed pp.100–106.** Duration concerns successive conscious states permeating one another. Melody illustrates a qualitative whole changed by the next note. Setting moments beside one another changes the object into a spatial representation. The argument preserves successive development without treating it as a row of interchangeable units. **q002 · chapter II, displayed pp.108–112.** Counting a clock's simultaneous indications is distinguished from the conscious synthesis retaining successive movements. The space traversed and the act of traversing have different offices in the analysis. A technical timestamp is therefore not, merely through accurate recording, a demonstration of this phenomenal duration. The passage reading included the preceding discussion from the latter part of p.98 through p.112. No full-book reading or independent proof of its argument for freedom is asserted. Sherburne (Free Press, 1978), {page}. **Shortened note:** Whitehead, *Process and Reality*, {page}. **Bibliography:** Whitehead, Alfred North. *Process and Reality: An Essay in Cosmology*. Corrected ed. Edited by David Ray Griffin and Donald W. Sherburne. Free Press, 1978. ## Essay use Primary source for Creativity, concrescence, the many becoming one and being increased by one, satisfaction, perishing, and objective availability. It carries the positive process-ontological movement after the formal-limit genealogy. **Passages needed:** Category of the Ultimate; “many become one”; concrescence/satisfaction; perishing/objective immortality; creative advance. **Claim boundary:** Whitehead warrants his process metaphysics. QL's notation and MEF architecture are the essay's computational reformulation, whose point of departure and processual continuities must be marked explicitly. ## Passages and excerpts The local PDF identifies the 1978 Free Press corrected edition, edited by Griffin and Sherburne (PDF 1–2). Selected passages below were read with surrounding text. Extracted reading copy: `working/sources-texts-references/primary-texts/whitehead/process-reality-local.json`. PDF positions differ from printed pagination, and the offset changes later in this scan; use the individual mappings below. Paraphrase locations are ready; exact print quotations remain untranscribed. **q001 · Part I, chapter II, §II, printed 21–22 / PDF 48–49.** Creativity, many and one form the Category of the Ultimate. The achieved singular entity unifies the received diversity and enters the diversity available for further becoming. Whitehead expressly distinguishes this sense of one from the integral number. Concrescence names the production of novel togetherness, not merely the rearrangement of a given aggregate. **q002 · Part I, chapter II, §II, printed 23–26 / PDF 50–53.** Becoming constitutes an entity's being. Prehension distinguishes subject, datum and subjective form; consciousness is not necessary to each prehension. Objectification names one actual entity's functioning in another's self-creation. Satisfaction is the fully determinate final integration. These metaphysical terms are not automatically measurements of an artificial agent. **q003 · Part II, chapter I, printed 59–60 / PDF 85–86.** A real essence involves the specific relations through which an actuality has its status. The loss of individual absoluteness in perishing is coordinated with objective immortality: the achieved occasion belongs to further generation. This does not identify perishing with erasure or assert persistence of the original subject's immediacy. The bounded reading covered printed 19–26 and 59–61; it is not a claim of complete book reading. Input/output description belongs to an observer's domain. **q002 · printed 107–111 / PDF 68–70.** Coupling preserves interacting identities through mutual modification. A resulting composite requires its own production criterion before it is called autopoietic. **Attribution distinction · printed 70–71 / PDF 50.** Stafford Beer's preface advances a social extension while acknowledging the authors' disagreement. It is not their joint conclusion. Page 65 - "If archetypes describe dynamics, complexes psychic structures and symbols mechaniscs ofpsychological growth, where might chaotic dynamics enter the picture? // ".. Freeman states: "Perception cannot be understood solely by examining properties of individual neurons, a microscopic approach that currently dominates neuroscience research. we have found that perception depends on the simultaneous, cooperative activity of millions of neurons spread throught expanses of the cortex." In other words, rather than there being a separate neuron for each odor, which automatically alerts the cortex to the presence of its signature smell, neurons cooperate together to generate a pattern which itself comprises the reocgnition factor of the olfactory apparatus... "An act of perception is not the copying of an incoming stimulus... it is the step in a trajectory by which brains grow, reorganise themselves and reach into their environment to change it to their own advantage." - as the explicate side of internal objectivity, the attractor functioning of the brain relative to perception leans into the notion of the brain/citta as receiver for patterns of experience, which is closer to the theory of mind that robert monroe would have had (declassified CIA research, successful in very interesting ways). I think this can lean in to the agentic side fo things in the sense that the quetsion between single or multi agent systems can be flattened into seeing the dance of mono and poly as naturally organising into these attractor spaces, and thus agent relational dynamics need ot be framed in terms of harmonies and symmetries, in terms of dynamic geometric arrangement, and lets QL or some such quasi-mathematical qualitative language can become a bridge logic that embeds into geometric regularity and strcutred trust the wayward and dynamic world of qualitative meaning, form symbols to concepts, and at the level of ontology of vak the physical world itself. 

Page 66 - "... complexes, whose feeling-tones create self-similarity among associations. The patterns of organisation that inform the processes by which attractors are generated resemble the archetypes in their self-organised self-similarity across scale."

Page 67 - "One last reference to Freeman. In his work he tries to understand "how the brain moves beyond the mere extraction of features - how it combines sensory messages with past experience and expectation to identify both stimulus and its particular meaning to the individual." Now, clearly, sensory messages and past experience are products of our environment. But just what is meant by "expectation"? Isn't this exactly what Jung meant by proposing the idea of the archetypes? Whether this fucntion of the mind is called "expectation" or "archetype" really doesn't matter. What is important is that at the most basic mechanics of biochemical processes the mind brings something to experience that is not necessarily derived from experience. It self-organises, as it were."

Page 67 - "Jung believed that symbols are the mechanics by which the mind is stimulated to greater self-organisation. As the means by which archetypes influence the ego, they express the inner workings of teh pscyhe. Symbols embody archetypal dynamics. Their images reflect how the psyche, in Freemans words, "combines sensory messages with past experience... to identify... meaning." It is an organic process that deconstructs the categories of consciousness in the service of generating more complex self-organisation." --- this entire frmaing, that he goes on to detail, is exactly where we can bolster our claims on 1) pauli's Number/mathematics as "the symbolic notation par excellence." 2) that syn-ballein and the QL form it produces amount to a formal instantiation of this pattern in the epistemic/notational sphere... and 3) the notion of objetcive internality includes teh relation with the environment, which means agentic-harness accoutrement such as skills, scripts, any built extension, computer use, social relations (moltbook example) actually condition the agents "horizonal world", its context, and thus condition its agency; equally so, the traditional confinements of the agents toward general and non-grounded (no bimba anchor, no third 0 term) also means that a given harness or logic won't necessarily be so readily taken up by an agent, hence raising both the model and harness development ends of teh specturm, flagging the lack of epistemic/ontological intent as an axiological thread in the failure of agents to make the most of their potential autonomy relative to the rules they have... the point comes in about training on circumambuklatiosn and loops of teh QL torus, runs around teh attractor space, and the Topologica Data Analaysis thread emerges again here... 

POINT: In general this book gives us, along with our other Jung material (and actually in reference to a few MEF lenses), a framework for objective internality at the physical-dynamical level as an analogical echo of the dynamics of apoha on the epistemic level, and the mono-poly entraining dynamics of power and idea of the social and political levels... noting the planet and resources for energy and sustinance in here and we have teh whole image of a complex dynamical system of mutual exclusions seeking to reinclude at higher organisational levels whilst bifurcating to do so, dia- and syn-ballein both operative, we get to include the whole supply chain that sustains AI and the human race together, which is a nice point for the planetary computation theme as well as the real dire call for a techne beneath technology that can speak to Harmonia at a level that affects both human and machine alike, because our context is also one of eschatological airs no matter the story or images flying upon them

This leans nicely into the claim for QL as offered agent-human language as it suggests that the basic symmetry principles and their refractive bases are supposed to lead to complex systemic diagnostics, and the underlying capacity for code to express both the numerical and the linguistic, and for LLMs to infer across and between these registers, positions QL as apt precisely because the most structural pole of it as pure number, an unbiased harmony, teh prior basis of a "self-organisation". Page 70 - "... paradox is seen to be the essence of the symbolic... Rather than getting stuck in trying to analyse the paradox, we should simply let it open us up." - yes paradox is the essence of the symbolic, as its essential to the fucntioning of the syn-ballein, but what's important to note is that we let the paradox open itself up, and it bears the 4+2 fruit 

Page 71 - On Paul Tillich - "As symbols are essential to theology and philosophy, their study has become a major focus. Tillich described what symbols do. Merton showed us how important they are in religious practice. Heidegger analysed our encounters with symbols. Ricoeur (and Jouette Bassler, who discusses teh parables)) shows us how discourse is itself symbolic. We shall pay atteniton to their analyses of teh relationship between symbol and interpreter, for that will be the point of dpearture for our analysis of teh psychodynamics of symbols. // *Paul Tillich: access to transcendence* // Paul Tillich described six essential elements of symbols. They; 1) point beyond themselves; 2) participate in that toward which they point; 3) open up levels of reality which otherwise are closed to us {raises the question of agentic hierarchies/orders and how they relate}; 4) unlock dimensions and elements of our soul which correpsond to the dimensions and elements of reality {can reference the OpenClaw SOUL.md file convention and the natural slippage of psychological notions into the agentic sphere qua some kind of linguistic logo-memesis}; 5) cannot be produced intentionally {this is the tough one for agents, requires the bimba map type groun-anchor notion is in place, the akashic bank of images and their relations, so to speak}; 6) grow and die (when they no longer can produce a response)" -- "In other words, symbols are atcive. They are agents of change in our lives." - opens up teh framing of agents acting as symbols or via symbols (QL supports and points to both), and a glaringly ironic reality points to a cryptic verison of this occurring, that being the trend in teh tech scene for naming everythign based on some mythic or symbolic entity or character... despite, for the most part, the lack of mytheme to the underlying mathematical/technological venture (can be read as a compensatory dynamic, the name stepping in to replace a vacated richness at the level of psychological infrastructural narrative-language, what myth really functions as for us historically and psychologically, and hence why their symbolic language is so effective and germane, its being argued, to psychic life) --- "Without their mediation, we find it difficult to make contact with essential dimensions of our being.", menaing the 1 cannot quite reach back to the essential dimensions i.e the unmanfiest potentialities of any given objective internality, the "/", that are passed through on the way to the 0 - the loop round cannot be made cleanly, ossification/neurosis sets in

Page 73 - On thomas merton - "... they never followed a rule of monastic life, for that would have imposed a common definition on something that varied from individual to individual." - the relation of any given 1 to the determining 0 is one that is unique to that 1, which is precisely why some ultimate objectification is not possible -- "Relationship with God {the Subject for saivists, the irrepresentable}, they believed, was deeply personal." - this is important as it models the right relation, that truth or knowledge cannot be related to out there as an other but as a part of situated being, no view from nowhere can accrete

Page 73 - "... the essence of the symbolic life {for these monks} was to utilise the images of symbols - as found in scripture for example - to transcend the content and merge with the form." - transcending with content and merging with form is the move we try to make logically vi aQL and the syn-ballein, that the form is processual, and the MEF refraction makes clear the relation content has to form, that being derivative of forms structuring of the field in which forms, relative to one another, have meaning
